raw_response:
Eight public references are useful for this recurring Kubernetes Job controller. The proposed applications below are design inferences from the references, not claims of deployment or measured improvement. The cutoff is October 2, 2020; only the explicitly dated cron package below is verified as pre-cutoff, and the final metrics implementation is later evidence.

1. **Kubernetes sample-controller informer/indexer/workqueue pattern** — https://github.com/kubernetes/sample-controller/blob/master/docs/controller-client-go.md
   Its informer callbacks, indexer and work queue provide an existing pattern for replacing repeated API polling with resource-change notifications and reconciliation against cached state. Apply it to schedule objects and child Jobs, mapping child events back to their owner. Reconciliation must tolerate stale observations and repeated notifications, wait for initial cache synchronization, and recover work after restart. **Date status: unknown; live source.**

2. **client-go delaying work queue** — https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/util/workqueue/delaying_queue.go
   AddAfter can place a schedule key on the work queue at its next calculated activation, while informer changes can trigger immediate work. The implementation uses a heap and timer for future entries. This queue is process-local, so restart recovery is necessary; duplicate future entries retain the earlier due time, meaning a wake must recheck the current schedule rather than assume a spec edit canceled the old timer. **Date status: unknown; attempts to verify the older tagged source failed.**

3. **robfig/cron v3.0.1** — https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/robfig/cron/v3
   ParseStandard and Schedule.Next supply cron parsing and next-occurrence calculation for a timed reconciliation. An alternative is a cron callback that only enqueues the controller key, keeping Job creation within Kubernetes reconciliation. Preserve the existing cron dialect, timezone and missed-run semantics; callback overlap wrappers do not enforce concurrency for cluster Jobs that outlive the callback. **Date status: pre-decision; the opened package page identifies v3.0.1, published January 4, 2020.**

4. **client-go workqueue MetricsProvider** — https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/util/workqueue/metrics.go
   Existing hooks cover queue depth, additions, wait latency, processing duration, retries and unfinished work. Register a provider and name the queue: the default provider is a no-op. Queue additions should not be reported as successful Job throughput, and time spent waiting in the queue does not capture lateness relative to the intended cron occurrence. **Date status: unknown; live implementation.**

5. **controller-runtime shared cache and timed reconciliation** — https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime/blob/main/doc.go and https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime/blob/main/pkg/reconcile/reconcile.go
   This is an alternative framework for watched-object events, shared cached reads, API writes and a RequeueAfter result that requests the next reconciliation after a duration. Use owned-Job events and the next scheduled occurrence as complementary triggers. A read immediately after a write may still see stale cached state, and framework adoption needs compatibility checks against the existing controller-manager and library versions. **Date status: unknown; live sources.**

6. **Kubernetes JobStatus completionTime and Complete condition** — https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/batch/job-v1/
   These fields identify successful Job completion and its timestamp, providing the input for a parent status field recording the latest observed successful completion. A practical adaptation is to retain the greatest successful completion timestamp from Jobs belonging to that parent. Check ownership, handle missing timestamps and status conflicts, and retain the aggregate before completed Jobs are pruned. Completion timestamps do not establish a guaranteed operation order. **Date status: unknown; live official API reference.**

7. **Prometheus histogram and summary guidance** — https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/histograms/
   Observation counts and sums support rate and average-latency calculations, while histogram buckets support aggregatable latency distributions. Instrument queue delay, reconciliation duration and intended-schedule-to-Job-creation delay separately, and define successful-creation throughput explicitly. Bucket selection affects the usefulness of quantiles, and summary quantiles cannot be averaged across workers. The page's newer native-histogram material is not established as available at the cutoff. **Date status: unknown; live documentation.**

8. **controller-runtime v0.25.2 reconciliation metrics** — https://pkg.go.dev/sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime%40v0.25.2/pkg/internal/controller/metrics
   This implementation illustrates result-labeled reconciliation counters and a reconciliation-duration histogram. It is useful as an instrumentation reference, although an internal package is not a public import contract and these metrics still differ from successful Job throughput and scheduling lateness. **Date status: post-decision; the opened package page states publication on September 30, 2026.**

A concrete composition to investigate is informer-driven observation plus cached reconciliation, a cron parser feeding a delayed queue, explicit success-status aggregation, and separate queue, reconciliation and schedule-delay measurements. controller-runtime is a framework alternative for parts of that composition. None of these references establishes that the resulting controller has been deployed or meets a particular throughput or latency target.
